summary.whatChanges: In the Hono RPC client, `$url()`/`$path()` now strip the synthetic `index` segment before substituting path params instead of after. This stops a param whose value is literally `index` from being deleted from the generated path. Tests cover nested, root-level, optional-param and query-string cases.
behaviorChanges: `client.docs[':page'].$path({param:{page:'index'}})` now returns `/docs/index` instead of having the `index` segment stripped
Root-level param values of `index` are preserved, yielding `/index`
`$url()` produces URLs retaining `index` param values, e.g. `http://localhost/docs/index?filter=test`
The synthetic `.index` proxy alias is still removed, so `client.files[':dir'].index` still gives `/files/123`
Query params are appended after index-stripping, so a query value cannot be affected by the stripping logic
risks: Stripping `index` from the un-substituted template could remove a literal `index` segment that a user intended to keep in a static route ending in `/index`
Behavior change is silent: code relying on the old stripping of `index`-valued params will now emit different paths
Only `$url`/`$path` were changed; the actual request path building elsewhere in the client may still use the old ordering, risking divergence between generated and requested URLs
